lens.csg: intersection of two spheres minus central cylinder

water.csg: roundedBox intersection freeSurfaceFill minus cableSweep minus18 bubble spheres

freeSurface.representation: Exact native non-rational cubic Bezier spans and original B-spline basis
freeSurface.normalRule: Normalize [-dz/dx,0,1] for the outward water normal
freeSurface.intersectionRule: Per relevant span solve z(s)-raySlope*x(s)-intercept=0; use derivative-root brackets; special case near-zero ray X. Validate membership against rounded box and cuts.

nativeBoundary.winding: Outward from water into the cable exclusion, native reversed surface orientation retained
nativeBoundary.scope: Only the native cable exclusion face; rounded box, free surface and bubble faces omitted
nativeBoundary.limitations: Tessellated native sweep, not an exact centerline-distance tube SDF; no independent continuous deviation proof

browserBinary.normalSource: BRepGProp_Face.Normal at each retained native Poly_Triangulation UV; exact BREP face orientation applied by BRepGProp_Face
browserBinary.normalOrientation: Outward from WATER toward the excluded cable void; native face is REVERSED. Do not flip these normals again.

opticalParts.modelPose: Module group X translation only; camera transform is separate

rigidTransformContract.shaderRule: Transform rays by each optical object inverse matrixWorld; normals use inverse transpose

limitations: Descriptor derives canonical source primitives and native OCC coefficients; it does not change CAD, meshes, package or renderer.
Source authoring formulas identify bubble centers and primitive prescriptions; free surface coefficients come from actual native BREP rather than re-evaluating the source sine formula.
Hybrid tracing must preserve cavity/port/bubble CSG membership and all entering/exiting intervals.
Cable sweep remains a finite native tessellation; coefficient and primitive intersections still require numerical tolerances.
This describes optical geometry only; screen-space opaque visibility, coatings, nested media transport and global lighting are separate renderer responsibilities.
